## Model

A multiple regression modeled the overall efficiency rating (Q37r, 1 = very poor, 5 = excellent) using Q31–Q34. Seven respondents lacked a valid Q37r rating, leaving 121 for analysis.

```{r}
library(haven)
library(knitr)

survey <- read_sav("Case 31 Data_efcu_4.sav")
names(survey) <- tolower(names(survey))
fit <- lm(q37_r ~ q31 + q32 + q33 + q34, data = survey)
model_summary <- summary(fit)
f <- model_summary$fstatistic
model_p <- pf(f[1], f[2], f[3], lower.tail = FALSE)
```

## Results

The model explained **30.1%** of the variation in ratings (adjusted R² = .276, F(4, 116) = 12.46, p < .001).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-coefficients
#| tbl-cap: "Multiple regression coefficients"
est <- coef(model_summary)
ci <- confint(fit)
kable(data.frame(
  Term = c("Intercept", "H5a: Confidentiality (Q31)",
           "H5b: Prompt processing (Q32)",
           "H5c: Services meet needs (Q33)",
           "H5d: Easy applications (Q34)"),
  b = est[, 1], SE = est[, 2], t = est[, 3],
  p = format.pval(est[, 4], digits = 3, eps = .001),
  "95% CI lower" = ci[, 1], "95% CI upper" = ci[, 2],
  check.names = FALSE
), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

### Hypothesis decisions

Each coefficient is the change in the efficiency rating per one-point increase in the predictor, holding the other three constant. Decisions use two-sided tests at α = .05.

- **H5a supported.** Confidentiality was positively associated with efficiency (b = 0.19, p = .036).
- **H5b supported.** Prompt loan processing had the largest positive coefficient (b = 0.31, p < .001).
- **H5c supported.** Meeting member needs was positively associated with efficiency (b = 0.29, p < .001).
- **H5d unsupported.** The estimate for ease of completing loan applications was inconclusive (b = −0.07, p = .390).

### Model diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-diagnostics
#| tbl-cap: "Model diagnostics"
vif <- diag(solve(cor(model.frame(fit)[, -1])))
kable(data.frame(
  Metric = c("Complete cases", "Residual standard error", "R²",
             "Adjusted R²", "Overall F", "Overall p",
             "Largest VIF", "Largest Cook’s distance"),
  Value = c(nobs(fit), round(model_summary$sigma, 3),
            round(model_summary$r.squared, 3),
            round(model_summary$adj.r.squared, 3), round(f[1], 2),
            format.pval(model_p, digits = 3, eps = .001),
            round(max(vif), 2), round(max(cooks.distance(fit)), 3))
), row.names = FALSE)
```

VIFs ranged from 1.07 to 1.40. The model treats the five-point outcome as approximately interval. Ratings clustered at the top of the scale (102 of 121 were 4 or 5).
